parties.name: Labour
parties.summary: Labour proposes a clean power mission targeting clean electricity by 2030, with a new publicly-owned company (Great British Energy), a National Wealth Fund, a windfall tax on oil and gas, no new exploration licences, and a Warm Homes Plan to cut household energy bills and reduce emissions.

citations.quote: clean energy by 2030 is Labour's second mission.
We will not issue new licences to explore new fields because they will not take a penny off bills, cannot make us energy secure, and will only accelerate the worsening climate crisis.

results.headline: Labour pledges clean energy superpower status by 2030
results.quote: Make Britain a clean energy superpower to cut bills, create jobs and deliver security with cheaper, zero-carbon electricity by 2030, accelerating to net zero.

parties.name: Conservative
parties.summary: The Conservatives commit to reaching net zero by 2050 through a pragmatic approach, including trebling offshore wind, scaling up nuclear power with new Small Modular Reactors, maintaining annual North Sea licensing rounds, and ensuring green levies on household bills are kept lower than 2023 levels.

citations.quote: We will deliver net zero by 2050, by: Sticking to our pragmatic, proportionate and realistic approach that eases the burdens on working people.
We will legislate to ensure annual licensing rounds for oil and gas production from our own North Sea

results.headline: Conservatives promise affordable transition to sustainable energy
results.quote: Delivering an affordable transition to domestic, sustainable energy.

results.headline: Conservative MP: decarbonise affordably without harming communities
results.quote: We believe in decarbonisation, but we need to do it in a way that people can afford and that does not trash our country in the process.

parties.name: Liberal Democrats
parties.summary: The Liberal Democrats propose achieving net zero by 2045, with a ten-year home energy upgrade programme, a rooftop solar revolution, removal of restrictions on wind and solar, a windfall tax on oil and gas super-profits, and restoring the UK's role as a global climate leader including returning development spending to 0.7% of national income.

citations.quote: Liberal Democrats are committed to cutting greenhouse gas emissions to net zero by 2045 at the latest.
Helping people with the cost of living and their energy bills by implementing a proper, one-off windfall tax on the super-profits of oil and gas producers and traders.

results.headline: Lib Dems commit to net zero by 2045
results.quote: Take the action needed now to achieve net zero by 2045.

results.headline: Lib Dem peer: cost of oil crisis exceeds cost of net zero
results.quote: The Climate Change Committee was clear last week that the cost of another oil price crisis would be greater than the cost of reaching net zero by 2050, so these Benches fully support the need to roll out renewables at a faster rate.

parties.name: SNP
parties.summary: The SNP demands devolution of energy powers to Scotland, calls on the UK Government to invest at least £28bn a year in the green economy, advocates an evidence-based case-by-case approach to oil and gas licences consistent with climate obligations, and presses for a Four Nations Climate Response Group to coordinate net zero targets across the UK.

citations.quote: The UK Government must invest at least £28bn a year in the green economy to deliver a step change in public and private investment in net zero and major investment in the domestic supply chain.
Establish a Four Nations Climate Response Group to agree climate plans across the UK that deliver on our net-zero targets and ensure the UK Government stops backtracking on climate ambition.

results.headline: SNP calls for fair and managed transition to net zero
results.quote: Deliver a fair and managed transition to net zero.
